diagram_name: Why Athens Looks the Way It Does
chapter_title: Day 13: Athens, Museums, Tutors, and the City Today
learning_objective: The learner will infer which event in modern Greek history, from 1967 to 2023, explains each of eight things a visitor can see in Athens today, matching at least 7 of the 8 correctly.
specification:
Type: timeline **sim-id:** modern-athens-timeline
**Library:** vis-timeline
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** infer
**Learning Objective:** The learner will infer which event in modern Greek history, from 1967 to 2023, explains each of eight things a visitor can see in Athens today, matching at least 7 of the 8 correctly. **Prerequisites:** the military dictatorship (junta), the Polytechnic uprising, the debt crisis, rescue loans and austerity, the 2015 sea crossings, the euro, the 2004 Olympics, Cyprus 1974, the 1999 earthquakes, the Athens Declaration, and the renaming of Greek coffee (all defined in Parts Three, Four and Five of this chapter). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the 8 sights, the learner selects one event on the timeline and commits the choice. A match is correct when it agrees with the "Correct event" column in Content (sight S6 accepts either of two events). Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Opening event descriptions on the timeline is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Everything a visitor notices in Athens is explained by ancient history. (2) Greek coffee is a different drink from Turkish coffee, so its name has nothing to do with politics. (3) The debt crisis was a single bad year rather than a decade that still shapes the city. (4) The refugees in Athens arrived mainly by air. **Instructional Rationale:** Inferring a cause from a present-day effect is an Understand task that makes the learner use the timeline rather than memorize it. Starting from things the learner can actually see on the street ties each date to a place, and the prediction is committed before the explanation is revealed. **Content:** Events on the timeline (all 14 are shown; some are context only): | ID | Date | Event | |---|---|---| | E1 | April 21, 1967 | Army colonels seize power; the military dictatorship begins | | E2 | November 14–17, 1973 | Polytechnic uprising; a tank breaks the main gate early on November 17 | | E3 | July 1974 | After a junta-backed coup in Cyprus, Turkish troops land on the island; the junta falls days later | | E4 | January 1, 1981 | Greece joins the European Economic Community | | E5 | August–September 1999 | Earthquakes in Turkey and Athens; rescue teams from each country help the other | | E6 | January 1, 2002 | Euro notes and coins replace the drachma | | E7 | August 2004 | Athens hosts the Olympic Games | | E8 | October 2009 | A new government reveals that the budget deficit was more than twice as large as reported | | E9 | 2010 | First rescue loan; deep cuts to wages, pensions, and public spending begin | | E10 | 2015 | More than 850,000 refugees and migrants reach Greece by sea, most crossing from Turkey | | E11 | June–July 2015 | Banks close; cash withdrawals limited to €60 a day; referendum on July 5 | | E12 | March 2016 | The European Union and Turkey agree on a deal to reduce the crossings | | E13 | August 2018 | Greece leaves its last rescue program | | E14 | December 2023 | Greek and Turkish leaders sign the Athens Declaration on friendly relations | Sights, in this order: | # | Sight shown to the learner | Correct event | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | S1 | Flowers at a twisted iron gate on Patission Street, and a march every November 17 | E2 | The gate is the one the tank broke in 1973, and the march remembers the uprising. | | S2 | A café menu offering "Greek coffee," where older Greeks remember ordering "Turkish coffee" | E3 | The name changed after 1974, when the war in Cyprus made the old name feel wrong to many Greeks. | | S3 | Prices in a Plaka souvenir shop written in euros | E6 | The euro replaced the drachma in everyday use in 2002. | | S4 | A metro line to the airport and a tram to the sea | E7 | Both were built for the 2004 Olympics. | | S5 | An older Athenian who remembers queuing at a cash machine for a daily €60 | E11 | Withdrawals were limited to €60 a day when the banks closed in 2015. | | S6 | Empty shops with "for rent" signs, and a family whose son now works in Germany | E9 (E8 also accepted) | The rescue loans brought cuts that shrank the economy by about a quarter and sent many young Greeks abroad; the 2009 revelation set them off. | | S7 | A Syrian bakery and an Afghan grocery in central Athens | E10 | Most of the newcomers arrived in the sea crossings of 2015, and some stayed. | | S8 | News photos of the Greek and Turkish leaders promising regular meetings | E14 | The Athens Declaration of 2023 committed them to regular contact. | **Provenance:** All dates and events are from this chapter's sections "The Athens Polytechnic Uprising", "The Greek Debt Crisis", "Daily Life in Athens", "Migration and Refugees Today", "Greek Coffee" and "Greek-Turkish Relations", and from Chapter 15's section "Athens as Modern Capital" (the Olympic rebuilding). The sights are composites of things visitors commonly see in Athens and must be labeled "Typical sights, not specific places". **Rules:** Each sight has exactly one correct event, except S6, which accepts E9 or E8. Events E1, E4, E5, E12 and E13 are context and are correct for no sight. An event may be chosen for more than one sight. The timeline shows all 14 events in date order from 1967 to 2023 from the start; event descriptions are visible on selection. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads sight S1 and the question "Which event explains this?" 2. The learner selects an event on the timeline and commits it. The selected event is highlighted. 3. The sim marks the match and shows the Why text. The matched event is labeled with the sight's number. 4. The learner continues through S2 to S8 in order. 5. At the end, the timeline shows all eight sights attached to their events, and the learner should notice that five of the eight fall between 2002 and 2023. **Feedback:** Eight sights in fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: " followed by the Why text. First wrong attempt: "Not this one. Look for an event that would leave this mark on the street." plus, for S2, "Think about what happened between Greece and Turkey." Second wrong attempt: the correct event is revealed with the Why text, and the sight counts as missed. A running score "n of 8 correct on the first attempt" is shown. **Starting State:** The timeline of 14 events from 1967 to 2023 is shown with no sights attached. Sight S1 is displayed with the question "Which event explains this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The junta began on April 21, 1967; the Polytechnic uprising ran November 14–17, 1973; the junta fell in July 1974; Greece joined the European Economic Community in 1981; the euro notes and coins arrived in 2002; the 2004 Olympics; the deficit revelation in October 2009; the first rescue loan in 2010; more than 850,000 sea arrivals in 2015; the €60 daily limit in 2015; the EU-Turkey deal of March 2016; the end of the rescues in August 2018; the 1999 earthquakes; the Athens Declaration of December 2023. Mastery is 7 of 8.
